page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 180 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, and is equipped with a large 260 MB L3 cache alongside 2 MB of L2 cache per core. It lacks integrated local NVMe storage and does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware vector and matrix extensions are a core architectural focus of this instance, featuring native support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8 instructions). Benchmark results reflect these capabilities, with PassMark extended instructions reaching 54,909.79 and encryption hitting 43,744.82. Geekbench testing shows robust compute execution with an 18,084 multi-core score, alongside top-tier text processing (2,925.0) and image processing (18,872.0). LLM inference on smaller models scales effectively using the available matrix extensions, processing 3,296.88 prompt tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

Throughput tests show strong performance in static web serving at 74.96 GB/s and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 288.36 GB/s. However, memory subsystems demonstrate more moderate metrics, recording 144.84 GB/s uncached read bandwidth and 61.98 GB/s write bandwidth, leading to an average PassMark memory score of 2,261.93. Redis SET operations average 60.15 million operations per second, indicating that raw memory bus operations represent a bottleneck compared to core computational throughput.

Without bundled ephemeral disk volumes, the instance relies entirely on external network-attached storage, which introduces an architectural dependency for disk-bound environments. The balanced vCPU-to-memory allocation makes the c4-standard-48 cost efficient for compute-dense microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, enterprise application servers, and CPU-driven machine learning inferencing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-48 is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, supported by 180 GB of RAM. Architecturally based on x86_64, the CPU includes advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, backed by a generous 260 MB L3 cache. Benchmarking indicates strong compute execution, reflected in a multi-core Geekbench score of 18,084 and high-throughput static web serving at 74.96 GB/s. Memory subsystem tests register at moderate levels, with uncached read speeds of 144.84 GB/s. The server provisions no local disks or discrete GPUs, requiring remote storage configurations. It is well suited for enterprise application workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, high-traffic web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines.
